short: Offering a complementary item alongside the purchase.
seoTitle: Cross-Selling — Meaning and Example for Businesses
metaDescription: Cross-selling offers a complementary product alongside what a customer is buying — a drink with a meal, a case with a phone, a dessert with a main.
definition: Cross-selling offers a complementary product alongside what a customer is buying — a drink with a meal, a case with a phone, a dessert with a main. It adds a separate item rather than upgrading the existing one.
bodyHtml:
Why Cross-Selling matters

Cross-sells are where basket size grows. They are also usually high-margin, since drinks, sides and accessories generally carry better margins than the anchor item.

How Cross-Selling works in practice

Pair items deliberately based on what already sells together, and place the suggestion where the decision happens — on the menu, at the counter, at checkout.

faq.question: How do I find good cross-sell pairs?
faq.answer: Look at what already appears together in bills, then make those combinations easier to choose.

faq.question: Is a combo the same as a cross-sell?
faq.answer: A combo is a pre-built cross-sell with a bundled price, which usually converts better than an ad-hoc suggestion.
